source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India Since Independence, Ch. 3 (Politics of Planned Development).

sections.heading: 1. The Idea of Planning
points: After Independence, India chose **planned development** to modernise the economy and remove poverty.
A **mixed economy** was adopted — combining **public and private sectors**.
The **Planning Commission (1950)** was set up; the **Five Year Plans** began (1951).

sections.heading: 2. Debates on Development
points: A key debate: **agriculture vs industry** — which to prioritise?
**Left vs right** debate: the role of the state vs the market; the pace and pattern of development.
The **Bombay Plan (1944)** showed even industrialists favoured a strong state role in planning.

sections.heading: 3. The First Two Plans
points: The **First Five Year Plan (1951–56)** — emphasised **agriculture, irrigation (dams — 'temples of modern India') and refugee rehabilitation**; based on the **Harrod-Domar model**.
The **Second Five Year Plan (1956–61)** — stressed **rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries and the public sector**; based on the **Mahalanobis model (P.C. Mahalanobis)**.
**Nehru** championed heavy industry and the public sector.

sections.heading: 4. Key Controversies and Green Revolution
points: The plans led to a strong industrial base but **neglected agriculture initially** → food shortages.
The **Green Revolution (mid-1960s)** boosted foodgrain output (but increased regional/class disparity).
**'White Revolution' (Operation Flood — Verghese Kurien, Amul)** transformed the dairy sector.
Debates continue on whether planning delivered equity.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: India = mixed economy; Planning Commission (1950); First Plan (1951).
First Plan (1951–56) = agriculture/irrigation (Harrod-Domar model).
Second Plan (1956–61) = heavy industry/public sector (Mahalanobis model).
Bombay Plan (1944) = industrialists favoured state-led planning.
Green Revolution (mid-1960s) = food self-sufficiency; White Revolution = milk (Kurien).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **First Plan = agriculture (Harrod-Domar)**; **Second Plan = heavy industry (Mahalanobis)**.
India adopted a **mixed economy** (public + private).
The **Mahalanobis model** guided the Second Five Year Plan.
**White Revolution (Operation Flood) = Verghese Kurien** (Amul, milk).
